req.title: Session persists across requests
req.statement: The system shall keep session['user_id'] populated across requests until logout for authenticated users.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-028 requires that session['user_id'] persists across multiple requests for authenticated users and is cleared on logout. Tests must cover: (1) positive — session persists across several authenticated requests; (2) negative — unauthenticated client has no session user_id; (3) boundary — session is present on the request immediately after login (boundary between unauthenticated and authenticated state) and is absent on the request immediately after logout (boundary between authenticated and unauthenticated state). Additional state-transition tests cover the full login→persist→logout cycle. All tests use exact-value assertions to kill comparison and constant mutations.

tests.name: test_session_persists_across_multiple_authenticated_requests
preconditions: App initialised with test database containing user Rahul (id=1, password=stone)
Client has not yet logged in
expected: Session cookie is present and non-empty across all requests
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

# Login
with client:
    r_login = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'}, follow_redirects=False)
    assert r_login.status_code == 302
    assert r_login.headers['Location'] == '/'

    # First subsequent request — session must carry user_id
    r_index = client.get('/', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r_index.status_code == 200

    # Second subsequent request — login_required must pass (session still valid)
    r_create = client.get('/create', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r_create.status_code == 200

    # Third subsequent request — session still valid
    r_index2 = client.get('/', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r_index2.status_code == 200

os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_unauthenticated_client_has_no_session_user_id
expected: GET /create returns HTTP 302 redirect to /auth/login (login_required fires)
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

with client:
    # No login — session must not contain user_id
    r = client.get('/create', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'

    # Confirm session has no user_id by checking that /create still redirects
    r2 = client.get('/create', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r2.status_code == 302
    assert r2.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'

os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_session_absent_immediately_after_logout
preconditions: App initialised with test database containing user Anjali (id=2, password=cloud)
expected: GET /create after logout returns HTTP 302 to /auth/login (session cleared)
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

with client:
    # Login
    r_login = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Anjali', 'password': 'cloud'}, follow_redirects=False)
    assert r_login.status_code == 302
    assert r_login.headers['Location'] == '/'

    # Boundary: request immediately after login — session must be active
    r_before = client.get('/create', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r_before.status_code == 200

    # Logout
    r_logout = client.get('/auth/logout', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r_logout.status_code == 302
    assert r_logout.headers['Location'] == '/'

    # Boundary: request immediately after logout — session must be cleared
    r_after = client.get('/create', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r_after.status_code == 302
    assert r_after.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'

os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_session_persists_across_login_state_transitions
preconditions: App initialised with test database containing users Rahul (id=1) and Anjali (id=2)
expected: State transitions: anon→auth→anon→auth all produce correct HTTP codes
Each authenticated state allows /create; each unauthenticated state blocks it
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

with client:
    # State 1: unauthenticated
    r = client.get('/create', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'

    # Transition: login as Rahul
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'}, follow_redirects=False)
    assert r.status_code == 302

    # State 2: authenticated as Rahul
    r = client.get('/create', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r.status_code == 200

    # Transition: logout
    r = client.get('/auth/logout', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r.status_code == 302

    # State 3: unauthenticated again
    r = client.get('/create', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'

    # Transition: login as Anjali
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Anjali', 'password': 'cloud'}, follow_redirects=False)
    assert r.status_code == 302

    # State 4: authenticated as Anjali
    r = client.get('/create', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r.status_code == 200

os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_wrong_credentials_do_not_establish_session
preconditions: App initialised with test database containing user Rahul (id=1, password=stone)
expected: Login returns HTTP 200 (re-renders login form with error)
GET /create returns HTTP 302 to /auth/login (no session established)
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

with client:
    # Wrong password — must NOT set session
    r_bad = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'wrongpassword'}, follow_redirects=False)
    assert r_bad.status_code == 200
    assert b'Incorrect password.' in r_bad.data

    # Session must not be established
    r_create = client.get('/create', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r_create.status_code == 302
    assert r_create.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'

    # Wrong username — must NOT set session
    r_bad2 = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'NoSuchUser', 'password': 'stone'}, follow_redirects=False)
    assert r_bad2.status_code == 200
    assert b'Incorrect username.' in r_bad2.data

    r_create2 = client.get('/create', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r_create2.status_code == 302
    assert r_create2.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'

os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_session_user_id_matches_logged_in_user
preconditions: App initialised with test database containing users Rahul (id=1) and Ishaan (id=3)
expected: session has no user_id after logout
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

with client.session_transaction() as sess:
    assert 'user_id' not in sess

with client:
    # Login as Rahul (id=1)
    client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'}, follow_redirects=False)
    with client.session_transaction() as sess:
        assert 'user_id' in sess
        assert sess['user_id'] == 1

    # Logout
    client.get('/auth/logout', follow_redirects=False)
    with client.session_transaction() as sess:
        assert 'user_id' not in sess

    # Login as Ishaan (id=3)
    client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Ishaan', 'password': 'stone'}, follow_redirects=False)
    with client.session_transaction() as sess:
        assert 'user_id' in sess
        assert sess['user_id'] == 3

os.unlink(path)
